questions.question: What should a content calendar actually include?
questions.answer_summary: Buffer's guide lists posting dates/times, captions, visual formats, asset links, and tracking URLs as the essential elements.

questions.question: How do I repurpose one piece of content across platforms?
questions.answer_summary: Later explains a single YouTube video can be cut into Instagram Reels, TikTok clips, and Pinterest pins to cover three platforms from one shoot.

questions.question: Do solo creators need to post every day?
questions.answer_summary: Later states consistency matters more than frequency — solo creators don't need daily posting, just an achievable, repeatable cadence.

questions.question: What's the actual step-by-step process for building a calendar?
questions.answer_summary: Buffer outlines a 7-step process: define strategy first, centralize ideas, tag/color-code content, set per-platform posting schedules, plan with a monthly/weekly view, balance timely vs. evergreen content, then analyze performance.

questions.question: What free templates exist for a content calendar?
questions.answer_summary: Buffer offers free templates in Buffer, Google Sheets, Canva, Notion, and PDF formats.

questions.question: How do I know which content pillar or format is working?
questions.answer_summary: Buffer recommends tagging/color-coding content by pillar, format, or status specifically so performance can be tracked later by category.

questions.question: Should posting times be the same across all three platforms?
questions.answer_summary: Buffer recommends setting distinct, consistent posting schedules ('Queue times') per platform rather than one blanket schedule.

questions.question: How do I balance viral/timely posts with evergreen content?
questions.answer_summary: Buffer advises mixing timely, viral content when available with consistently scheduled 'bread and butter' evergreen posts.

questions.question: What tool centralizes planning across multiple platforms?
questions.answer_summary: Later positions its centralized content calendar as letting creators plan and schedule across channels from one place, with a shared media library for assets.

questions.question: How far in advance should content be planned to save time?
questions.answer_summary: Later recommends blocking dedicated time to plan content 'en masse' rather than reactively, to save creation hours over time.

questions.question: How do solo creators avoid content chaos across three platforms?
questions.answer_summary: Later frames a single centralized calendar as the fix for content becoming scattered and unmanageable across separate platforms.
